title: No Scripture makes justification an eternal decree; it follows faith and the Spirit
source_text: XIV. Et certe si quis percurrat omnia Scripturae loca, ubi de justificatione hominis mentio fit, ne unum quidem reperiet, ubi vel minimum indicium appareat, per justificationem intelligi aeternum quoddam Dei decretum. Imo vix unus est, ubi non occurrat aliquid, unde facile colligere liceat, per illam designari beneficium quoddam in tempore collatum, quodque hominis fidem & conversionem sequitur, non vero antecedit. Nam, ut omittam plurima illa loca, ubi dicimur, ex fide & per fidem justificari, & credere in Christum ut ex fide justificemur, quibus in locis fides manifeste proponitur, tanquam aliquid ad justificationem praerequisitum, justificatio semel tribuitur Spiritui Sancto in electos Dei effuso, & per illum fieri dicitur; argumento manifesto neminem, juxta mentem Scripturae Sacrae, justificatum esse, priusquam Spiritum Sanctum a Deo acceperit. Nam Tit. 3. v. 6. testatur Apostolus Deum in nos Spiritum Sanctum abunde effudisse, ut ex gratia ipsius haeredes simus secundum spem vitae aeternae. Et 1 Cor. 6. v. 11. fideles quos alloquitur dicit sanctificatos & justificatos fuisse, in nomine Domini Jesu, & per Spiritum Dei nostri.
pass_a_gloss: And certainly if anyone runs through all the places of Scripture where mention is made of man's justification, he will not find even one where the least indication appears that by justification an eternal decree of God is meant. Indeed there is scarcely one where something does not occur from which one may easily gather that by it is designated a certain benefit conferred in time, which follows a person's faith and conversion and does not precede them. For, to omit those many places where we are said to be justified from faith and through faith, and to believe in Christ that we may be justified from faith—in which places faith is plainly set forth as something prerequisite to justification—justification is once attributed to the Holy Spirit poured out on God's elect, and said to be done through him; by a clear argument that according to the mind of Sacred Scripture no one has been justified before he has received the Holy Spirit from God. For in Titus 3:6 the Apostle testifies that God richly poured out the Holy Spirit on us so that by his grace we might be heirs according to the hope of eternal life. And in 1 Cor 6:11 he says the believers he addresses were sanctified and justified in the name of the Lord Jesus and by the Spirit of our God.
pass_b_english: Scripture never equates justification with an eternal decree.
It is a temporal gift after faith/conversion, done by the poured-out Spirit (Tit 3; 1 Cor 6).
